claude.performance_metric: $717M cumulative Wholesale goodwill impairment (goodwill fell $432M→$10M within ~21 months); several acquired Retail banners disposed as discontinued ops, remaining 73-store Retail retained (divestiture announced then reversed)
claude.rationale: p4=1: the slice documents realized product-line/operations incoherence — several acquired Retail banners (Hornbacher's, Shop 'n Save, Shop 'n Save East, certain Shoppers) were disposed as discontinued operations, $40M of closed-property reserve charges related to divestiture of retail banners were taken, and UNFI announced then reversed its intention to divest the acquired Retail tier while reorganizing Wholesale into four regions — showing the acquired product lines could not be cleanly aligned with operating processes over time. p5=1: the slice documents a realized process/organization fracture, with the FY2021 risk-factor specifically stating "the terms of some legacy Supervalu collective bargaining agreements may limit our ability to increase efficiencies," directly tying operational efficiency against the acquired workforce/labor organization. t1 and t2 are uncertain because the slice contains no documented evidence about the controlling-intent archetype or reconciliation of two value-capture models over time.

gemini.performance_metric: $717 million cumulative goodwill-impairment charges against the Wholesale reporting unit
gemini.rationale: There is no documented evidence of disruption specifically at the product/process interface, so p4_pathway is coded 0. However, there is documented friction at the process/organization interface, as the FY2021 10-K explicitly notes that 'the terms of some legacy Supervalu collective bargaining agreements may limit our ability to increase efficiencies,' indicating organizational constraints on operational integration, supporting a 1 for p5_pathway.

grok.rationale: p4 is coded 0 because the slice documents Wholesale reorganization into geographic regions, partial Retail-banner disposals as discontinued operations, and a later retention of Cub Foods/Shoppers, but does not document product-line/operations incoherence or failure to align acquired products with operating processes over time. p5 is coded 0 because the only organization-facing item is FY2021 risk-factor language that legacy Supervalu CBA terms 'may limit our ability to increase efficiencies,' which is prospective risk wording rather than a realized operations-vs-organization fracture; that specific legacy-Supervalu attribution is dropped by the FY2022 filing.
